rebalance_callable_by_any_caller.meaning: rebalanceFunds() has no access control modifier, so any caller can invoke it

custodian_is_contract_addr.meaning: the custodian address is a contract capable of executing code during the external transfer

vault_token_is_callback_enabled.meaning: the vault token is an ERC777 or callback-enabled token that can invoke a callback during transfer

redemption_reduced_balance_before_rebala.meaning: a user redemption via processTransfer() reduced the vault balance before the attacker calls rebalanceFunds()

excess_drained_twice.meaning: re-entrancy during the external _vaultToken.transfer(custodian, excess) call causes excess funds to be drained twice
excess_drained_twice.checkpoint: after the re-entrant external transfer to the custodian

assumptions: The external transfer to the custodian is _vaultToken.transfer(custodian, excess) and is the point at which the malicious custodian re-enters.
The custodian contract is the re-entering party during the external transfer.
The excess amount is the value transferred to the custodian in the rebalanceFunds() call.

unresolved.description: Report gives no concrete excess amount or balance values, so the double-drain is represented only by the report-stated occurrence of excess being drained twice.

Report states reentrancy and double-drain are conditional on the custodian being a contract and the token being ERC777/callback-enabled; these are encoded as preconditions rather than established facts.

limitations: The plan formalizes only the double_drain impact; spam, DoS delay, and under-collateralization impacts are not covered here.
The double-drain occurrence is a report-stated qualitative outcome without numeric magnitudes.
Whether a real transaction occurred is not established; the scenario is a possible attack vector.
